## B351-R1-01: the first turn states authority from the type, not the role

**Blocking correctness, P2.** `crates/daemon/src/community/first_turn.rs:309-312` renders `Carries authority: yes|no.` using `def.authority()`. That reads the type's descriptive flag, not the position the seat will hold. `crates/daemon/src/community/holders.rs:9-23` derives that position from the role id; `directory.rs:1868-1874` uses it when indexing the assignment. Types are labels and grant nothing, as the bundled concepts page explicitly explains.

A private regression probe checked that both documents pass `types::check_role`, checked their actual `seat_role_for` result, and called the unmodified `assemble`:

| Role | Type | Assigned position | New first-turn sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release-helper` | `pa` | `worker` | `Carries authority: yes.` |
| `pa` | `worker` | `pa` | `Carries authority: no.` |

The probe fails on both mismatches. These are supported role/type combinations, not an exploit or a proposed permission model: a newly started seat is told the wrong fact about what it may do. The old type part did not make this explicit authority claim. This matters especially after moving the fuller explanation behind the page pointer.

**Fix:** if the sentence describes the seat's actual authority, derive it from the existing role-id/position mechanism, never `meta.type`. Alternatively, make it explicitly a description of which position the type is intended for, retaining the statement that the type itself grants nothing. Add the role-id/type mismatch cases to the existing first-turn test. No authorization behavior should change.
